planDeadlineReview.numericOrigin: Only the implementation progress record specifies the voice100ms number. Line303 calls it the initial database wait for the audio domain; line319 explicitly leaves applicability to disk performance, slow disk and CPU congestion to P0/Q25. The module11 voice product requirements and API15 contract do not separately promise every upload reserve/publish will complete within100ms.
planDeadlineReview.separateBudgets: Do not conflate the100ms audio-domain database wait, the100ms authority-memory coherency barrier, P95 desktop hide100ms/P99 250ms, file-validation wall30s/CPU10s, and actual transport upload120s. They protect different phases and have different evidence requirements.
planDeadlineReview.currentSharedPolicy: VoiceService.repository_mode uses100ms for reserve/publish as well as native driver/control metadata and other repository calls. That is the existing implementation policy whose behavior is recorded; API15 reuses VoiceService but does not require one numerical timeout for all these operation classes.
planDeadlineReview.whenReserveTakesOver100ms: Under current code the caller remains bounded. If the writer ticket result is unknown at timeout, failing closed in the voice runtime, blocking further positive effects and preserving any possibly committed asset for reconciliation is consistent with progress10:303 and API15:34. It must not claim a definite failure/noCOMMIT or automatically replay the upload. The plan does not establish that ordinary NTFS guarantees completion under100ms; a slow but correct fsync can legitimately drive this existing policy to UNKNOWN.
planDeadlineReview.busyVsFaulted: The source needs stage-specific classification. A pure authority-update wait timing out before issuing SQL is StorageError::Busy and should not invalidate the voice runtime (progress10:328). A writer timeout/indeterminate path invalidates the voice runtime through VoiceService.conclude. VoiceRepositoryError::Faulted is not automatically the process HealthGate::Faulted.
planDeadlineReview.globalHealthNuance: Transaction evaluate deadline expiry returns before authority update; precommit failure with successful SQL rollback and publisher.rollback restores old Healthy. Message::Transaction does not blanket mark every Indeterminate result globally faulted. Actual commit ambiguity, rollback failure, worker panic or failed authority publication do mark the HealthGate faulted. This matches08:35; the blanket Indeterminate check in worker_loop belongs to Message::Login, not transaction voice tasks.
planDeadlineReview.shouldNativeAndWebShare100ms: They must share exact original lease/generation, single-writer consistency, bounded ownership and failclosed effect gates. They do not inherently need the same numeric wait. Native feeding/stop paths cannot block behind long upload/disk/KDF work; an upload metadata operation on a bounded worker could have a separately finite, measured admission/COMMIT budget without allowing UI/audio to wait. This would be a deliberate budget-policy change with explicit P0/Q25 calibration, not an ad hoc increase to make the failed test pass.
planDeadlineReview.recommendedDecisionNow: Keep existing numbers and all assertions while collecting root diagnostic phase/elapsed/error data. Do not blame NTFS, declare a permit bug, weaken the final201, add automatic retry or count an old PASS as causal evidence. If the trace proves normal disk commits repeatedly exceed100ms, treat it as a real availability/design constraint of the shared policy; decide whether to optimize bounded writer work or explicitly separate upload-metadata and native-control budgets, with corresponding plan updates and deadline/cancellation/lateCOMMIT tests. Preserve100ms for the native/control path unless separately justified.
planDeadlineReview.notAChangeRequest: Reviewer did not edit code or plan, did not execute the temporary diagnostic binary, and does not assert which path caused the observed failure.
